CORRECTED: initial pull used a date-string BETWEEN filter that silently excluded ~10 contacts created late on 9 Aug; all HubSpot figures below use explicit UTC boundaries (>= 3 Aug 00:00 UTC, < 10 Aug 00:00 UTC), confirmed against a direct 228-contact export. UPDATED 9 Aug: 8 contacts (100+ employees, senior-or-above) were manually promoted to MQL in HubSpot as an ICP-fit sweep. 5 (Andrew Inwood, Trevor De Vries, Adam Donnelley, Andrew Britz, Nathan Mcqueen — State of AI ABO campaign) were created within the Week 32 window and belong here on both counts. The other 3 (Liem Nguyen, Dave Jenkinson, James Tidey) were created 28 May–31 Jul — BEFORE this week — and are counted here at explicit user direction, not because their createdate places them in this cohort. Their createdate was not altered; this is a deliberate exception to the report's stated 'Week = contacts created that week' methodology, flagged here for anyone reconciling against HubSpot directly.

highlight.html: Volume rebounded hard, organic quality didn't follow. 228 new contacts (+133% vs Week 31), but the increase is almost entirely the Facebook "State of AI 2026" relaunch (129 contacts) plus a wave of Sugarwork case-study campaigns (40 contacts, ~36% MQL). 188 of 228 are newsletter subscribers. MQL+ reads 25 (11%*) — including 2 internal QA/test records and 8 enterprise/senior contacts manually promoted after an ICP-fit review, 3 of which (Liem Nguyen, Dave Jenkinson, James Tidey) were created before this week and are included here by explicit direction, not by their actual creation date. Organic Week 32 MQL+ is 15. The week's only opportunity, Ben Criddle (Group Sourcing Manager, AU), was sales-created via CRM, not marketing-attributed. DecidrOS produced zero contacts for a third straight week.

stateOfAiSize.verdict: LinkedIn pulls enterprise, Meta pulls SMB — sharply. 100% of LinkedIn's State of AI leads are 200+ employees (median 5k+) vs 13% on Meta (median 1–20). To reach the 250+ ICP, scale LinkedIn — though Meta still has a real enterprise tail (12 leads at 500+).

observations.html: Volume rebounded but organic quality didn't follow. 228 contacts (+133% vs Wk 31) yet organic MQL+ is 15 (7%) — the reported total of 25 (11%) includes 8 manually-promoted contacts, 3 of which weren't even created this week (see note below).

"State of AI 2026" Facebook relaunch drove 129 of 228 contacts (57%) and shows 7 MQLs — all 7 were manually promoted after an ICP-fit review (100+ employees, senior-or-above), not organic engagement; 2 of the 7 (CBO row) were created before this week. The campaign's organic MQL rate is still effectively 0%.

Sugarwork case-study campaigns were the week's best organic-quality performer. 5 Facebook variants converted 12 of 33 new Sugarwork leads to MQL (36%) purely through lifecycle progression, no manual intervention (a 13th Sugarwork MQL, Dave Jenkinson, was added via the same manual sweep and predates this week).
DecidrOS produced zero new contacts for a third straight week. The demand engine remains paused with no replacement campaign in market.
No marketing-sourced SQL or opportunity this week. The lone opportunity, Ben Criddle (Group Sourcing Manager, AU), was sales-created via CRM.
Channel concentration: Paid Social is 62% of contacts (142 of 228). Offline/import contributes 35% (79, mostly the ongoing bulk-import tail), Direct just 3%.

10 of the 25 reported MQL+ contacts don't reflect organic lifecycle progression. 2 are internal QA/test records ("QA-HMS Test", "QA-Fixed Test") and 8 are a manual ICP-fit promotion (100+ employees, senior-or-above) — of which 3 (Liem Nguyen, Dave Jenkinson, James Tidey) were created before this week and are counted here at explicit user direction, not by actual creation date. Organic MQL+ for Week 32 is 15.

LinkedIn Ads spend data was unavailable this week — Supermetrics returned "Member is restricted" for both connected LinkedIn accounts. Lead counts (13) are HubSpot-only; re-authenticate the connection to restore spend/cost-per-lead reporting.

leadQuality.html:
No marketing-sourced SQL this week — the story is volume vs. quality across campaigns. Compare the two paid pushes that drove this week's volume:

High volume, no qualification: "State of AI 2026" Facebook relaunch (ABO + CBO) — 133 platform leads, $3,338 spend, 0% MQL. A broad-reach report download that hasn't yet produced a qualified lead.
Lower volume, real quality: Sugarwork subsea-company case-study campaigns (5 variants, AUS + USA) — 36 platform leads, $2,757 spend, 17–36% MQL per campaign, best of the week.
Highest intent: Technology Partners demo-leads campaign — just 3 contacts, but 100% MQL, consistent with direct demo requests outperforming awareness/report downloads.

Sales generated this week's only opportunity (Ben Criddle) independent of any campaign — a reminder that marketing volume and sales pipeline moved on separate tracks this week.
